title: Prefix-aware caching strategy and safe rollout for adaptive TTL & batching recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce actionable prefix/key design guidance, a hit-rate modelling workflow, automated TTL/policy tuning heuristics, and a safe apply + rollback plan for applying adaptive KV/prefix cache configs. This ticket bundles the modeling experiments, config schema, canary gating, and runbook required to push a conservative adaptive TTL feature to production. Scope: prefix key normalization rules, per-prefix TTL candidate ranges, admission policies (LFU/LRU/hybrid), batching-aware cache semantics, simulation harness, and canary automation. Out of scope: end-to-end UI in Console; that will be a follow-up (PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria:
- Simulation tool can ingest 14 days of historical request logs and output expected hit-rate and token-cost delta by prefix bin.
- Family of TTL policies (short, medium, long) with concrete numeric ranges and per-prefix assignment heuristics documented.
- Deployable config schema with feature-flag gating and canary orchestration (1%,5%,25%,100%).
- Automatic rollback triggers and a documented runbook.
- Backend e2e tests and a small perf benchmark (P50/P95/P99) showing no >5% regression in tail latency during 25% rollout in staging.
- PR with design doc, simulation artifacts, and unit/integration tests merged.
implementation_plan: 1) Build hit-rate simulator that replays historical traces with configurable TTLs, admission policy, and batch boundaries. 2) Run clustering on prefixes by request frequency and inter-arrival distribution to produce prefix bins (hot, warm, cold, bursty). 3) Define TTL candidates per bin and simulate cost/hitrate/latency tradeoffs. 4) Implement config schema (json) and server-side apply path with atomic snapshot and validation. 5) Add feature-flag + canary controller in runtime orchestration allowing traffic split per workspace/region. 6) Instrument dashboards and alerts for safety metrics. 7) Run staged rollout in prod with automated rollback hooks.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0 (staging): run simulation vs staging traces, smoke tests.
- Stage 1 (canary-1): enable 1% of traffic in a synthetic workspace; monitor 24h.
- Stage 2 (canary-5): expand to 5% across low-risk workspaces; monitor 48h.
- Stage 3 (canary-25): expand to 25% including mid-volume customers; run A/B comparison for 72h.
- Stage 4 (gradual): ramp to 100% if metrics stable.
Rollback triggers: cache-hit-rate drop >10% for a prefix bin AND token-cost increase >5% for the same window; P99 latency regression >10%; 5xx increase >2x baseline. Rollback mechanism: config snapshot restore via single API call and immediate circuit-break to previous allocation.
metrics: Primary: cache hit-rate delta (by prefix bin), token cost per request, overall token spend, P99 latency, 5xx rate. Secondary: cache eviction rate, admission rejection ratio, average batch size, KV CPU/GPU utilization. Monitor windows: 1m, 5m, 1h, 24h. Alert tiers defined for canary and full rollout.
experiments_summary:
We ran three simulation runs on 14-day production traces (sanitized).
- Baseline: existing static TTL=600s for all prefixes. Baseline hit-rate (weighted) = 0.41, avg token cost per request = 1.00x.
- Policy A (bin-based TTL: hot=180s, warm=900s, cold=7200s): expected weighted hit-rate = 0.58 (+41%), estimated token cost per request = 0.83x (-17%), small increase in eviction churn for hot bins.
- Policy B (adaptive admission: LFU-like promotion + short sticky TTL for bursty prefixes): expected hit-rate = 0.61 (+49%), token cost per request = 0.79x (-21%), slightly increased memory footprint for LFU counters ~+6%.
Recommendation: start with Policy A for safety and move to Policy B after 25% canary if counters stable. Full simulation details and plots in design doc link.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: mis-keying causes cache fragmentation and lower hit-rate. Mitigation: enforce canonicalization library (lowercase, sorted param set, hashed variable-length params) and add preflight validation that rejects configs that increase unique-key cardinality >5% in simulation.
Risk: canary noise from short-lived spikes. Mitigation: require stability across 72h for canary-25 before wider rollout and incorporate burst detection that temporarily disables adaptivity for prefixes with coefficient-of-variation >2.
Risk: operator error during apply. Mitigation: atomic snapshot + dry-run validation, required code owner approval, and one-click rollback API.
Risk: storage pressure from LFU metadata. Mitigation: cap counters, use approximate counting (Count-Min sketch) and conservative promotion thresholds.
notes: Decision log: prefer conservative numeric TTLs and binning to start; avoid per-request micro-TTL changes until we have live telemetry.
Follow-ups: Console UX ticket for exposing per-workspace canary controls (PM to own).
SRE: add a runbook entry under Oncall playbooks for cache-rollout incidents.
